selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What are the two medicines named at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: One is trust in Allah together with patience, and the other is depending on the Creator’s power while being confident in His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage support the claim that trust in Allah removes fear?
questions.answer: It says a person who knows his own weakness and leans on the Lord of all creation has no real reason to panic, because he entrusts his affairs to the One whose command is always effective.

questions.question: What response to severe hardship is described for a believer?
questions.answer: He remembers that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him, then places his reliance on his Merciful Lord.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can weakness become something positive?
questions.answer: When a person recognizes his helplessness before Allah, that weakness becomes a reason to seek nearness, protection, and inward peace rather than pride in himself.

questions.question: What example is given to explain the sweetness found in helplessness and fear?
questions.answer: The example is of a baby who feels vulnerable and, because of that need, finds comfort and safety in the mother’s care.

questions.question: Why is the baby example not the final point of the argument?
questions.answer: Because the passage says a mother’s mercy is only a tiny sign of Allah’s far greater mercy.

questions.question: What kind of fear is presented as beneficial in this passage?
questions.answer: It is reverent fear of Allah that pushes a person to seek refuge in Him, not hopeless terror.

questions.question: How did the wise respond to their lack of personal power?
questions.answer: They openly admitted they had no independent strength and turned to Allah for support.

questions.question: What attitude did the wise take toward their own strength?
questions.answer: They denied any independent power in themselves and sought help from Allah alone.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the first medicine made up of?
questions.answer: It consists of trusting Allah and being patient.

questions.question: What is the second medicine made up of?
questions.answer: It consists of relying on Allah’s power and being confident that His wisdom is sound.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect human weakness with peace instead of despair?
questions.answer: Because weakness becomes a reason to depend on Allah rather than on one’s limited self.

questions.question: What belief about Allah makes reliance reasonable in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah is described as having absolute authority and power, so turning to Him is the most secure response.

questions.question: What words is the believer said to remember during disaster?
questions.answer: He remembers that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: What emotional change takes place when someone knows Allah properly?
questions.answer: Fear and weakness are transformed into a source of comfort because they lead the person to divine refuge.

questions.question: What lesson is taught through the image of the infant?
questions.answer: True sweetness can be found not in self-sufficiency, but in recognizing need and seeking shelter in mercy.

questions.question: How does the passage rank divine mercy in relation to a mother’s mercy?
questions.answer: A mother’s tenderness is presented as only a very small reflection of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What deeper point does the passage make after giving the example of the mother?
questions.answer: It teaches that if even created mercy gives comfort, then turning to Allah’s mercy gives far greater peace.

questions.question: What problem in the human condition are the two medicines meant to address?
questions.answer: They address fear, helplessness, and the burden of facing hardship with only one’s own limited ability.

questions.question: What are the two medicines called in the passage?
questions.answer: They are trust in Allah with patience, and reliance on His power with confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the question of whether these medicines really work?
questions.answer: It gives a strong affirmation that they do work and then explains why.

questions.question: What kind of person is described as being free from crippling fear?
questions.answer: A person who knows his weakness and relies on the Lord of the world.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention Allah’s command that instantly brings things into existence?
questions.answer: To show that the One being trusted has unlimited power and is fully able to help.

questions.question: What does the believer do mentally and spiritually when calamity strikes?
questions.answer: He remembers his belonging to Allah, his return to Him, and then entrusts himself to divine care.
